title: Michael Jackson Estate Submits $115K Fee Bill As Paris Jackson Legal Fight Escalates | Hollywood News - News18
text: The legal wrangling over Michael Jackson ’s estate is far from cooling off. In a fresh court filing, attorneys for the estate’s executors have asked a Los Angeles judge to sign off on more than $115,000 in legal costs tied to their latest courtroom win. The paperwork, filed on Friday, January 9, lays out what the executors say they are owed after successfully shutting down a legal challenge brought by Jackson’s daughter, Paris Jackson, who is one of the estate’s beneficiaries. $115,000 Bill Put Before The Court Lawyers representing executors John Branca and John McClain submitted a detailed breakdown of fees and expenses connected to an anti-SLAPP motion they filed last year. That motion was granted by the court in November, reports People. According to the filing, the executors are seeking $93,924.63 in attorneys’ fees and $1,238.39 in related costs tied directly to the anti-SLAPP motion. The remaining amount reflects additional expenses connected to recovering those funds. The filing explains that the purpose of the January 9 submission was to “account for the fees and costs incurred by the Executors in connection with the anti-SLAPP motion so that the Court can determine the amount of the award." Because the executors won that motion, they argue they are legally entitled to reimbursement. When the court granted the anti-SLAPP motion, it struck down allegations Paris had raised in a petition filed in July. Paris Jackson Pushes Back Paris’ camp sees the filing very differently. Her spokesperson framed it as another attempt by the executors to extract money from the estate. According to People, he said, “For months, Paris Jackson has worked to address what appear to be troubling discrepancies and financial irregularities in the administration of her father’s estate." “It’s no surprise the executors and their lawyers are using every tool at their disposal to take even more money from the Jackson family and use it to line their own pockets. Paris remains undeterred and will continue fighting for transparency, accountability and fairness for her family." Paris shares beneficiary status in the estate with her brothers, Prince, 28, and Bigi, 23. Long-Running Dispute Over Money And Control The clash is part of a wider dispute that has been simmering for months. In November, Paris filed a new legal document accusing Branca and McClain of abusing their roles as executors to enrich themselves. She alleged that in 2021 alone, they collected more than $10 million in compensation from the estate, an amount she claimed was “more than double the amount distributed to any beneficiary from the family allowance," informs People. The executors have pushed back hard. In a motion filed in October, they stated that Paris has received approximately $65 million in benefits from the estate. They also point to the estate’s turnaround after Jackson’s death in 2009, when he was more than $500 million in debt. In their filing, the executors said they transformed a struggling operation into a “powerhouse and a force in the music business." The judge now has to decide whether the full $115,000 bill gets approved.
